chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit, from 'Amr ibn Jami', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no man who pays the zakat such that it decreases from his wealth, nor does anyone withhold it such that it increases in his wealth.

key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam; a percentage of wealth given to designated recipients
key_terms.زادت: Increased, grew — the ironic result of withholding zakat is that it does not actually increase wealth
key_terms.نقصت: Decreased, diminished — used here to refute the assumption that giving charity reduces wealth

ai.seo_question: Does paying zakat decrease wealth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that paying zakat never truly diminishes a person's wealth, and withholding it never genuinely increases it. This hadith addresses the psychological barrier to charity — the fear of financial loss — by affirming that divine blessing (baraka) compensates and multiplies the wealth of the one who fulfills this obligation. The original audience, early Muslim communities forming the foundations of Islamic jurisprudence, would have understood this as a theological assurance grounded in the principle that God does not diminish what is given in His path.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashhab, from Ibn Baqah, from Muaz Bin Sa’ib, from Amro Bin Jumi’e, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is none from a man who pays the Zakāt, he would be reducing from his wealth, nor anyone preventing it, so it would increase his wealth (in any way)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Khashshab from ibn Baqqah from Mu’adh ibn Thabit from ‘Amr ibn Jumay‘ who has said the foiiowing: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
there is no one who pays his zakat who then experiences any decrease in his wealth. Also no increase takes place in the wealth of one who refuses to pay zakat which is due on him.”
